We seem to have a "hop shortage" every few years when prices start to come down.

That being said, that's not the real trouble in the craft beer industry. It's the "Brewery Bubble".

Most of these craft breweries are not being opened by die hard, dedicated, for-the-love-of-beer fanatics. They're being opened by investment groups and VC firms. 5 years ago, opening a brewery was like a license to print money as the craft beer revival took off. There wasn't much local/regional competition, quality was high, and novelty commanded a premium price. The finance people jumped in and most of the originators of the "revival" have been bought out and exited the game.

Now, margins are thin, at best. Regional and local competition is staggering (I have 10+ breweries within a 30 minute drive) and the novelty no longer commands the kind of premium pricing since you can get it just about everywhere. You're going to see the bottom drop out of the craft beer market here in another 2-3 years when all these investment guys pull their money back out since the returns simply are not there anymore.
The market is over saturated with hop heavy beers. Maybe the upside of this is we beer drinkers will start seeing more offerings of other styles.
